scope: one offline 512x512 embedded-texture prototype; no runtime integration or catalog admission

implementation.atlas: 512x512 PNG made once from the inspected 4096x4096 TGA; source UVs, normals, winding, and silhouette retained

glb.license: CC0 / Asset Quest; preserved License.txt SHA-256 ad0c0abda67dae90291d8d6e2fcb07c841bb210cdedfa9dfdedae605bd8f66c6

firstAttempt.finding: The uniform pink panel was blank because the first fixture version assigned a single material as a one-element array on ungrouped geometry. The directory is immutable and is excluded from the visual verdict.

checks: Original full 4096x4096 TGA and embedded 512x512 PNG both loaded.
Uniform pink material rendered with mapRemoved=true and color #ff69b4.
Front and rear renders had no page errors or external requests.
Original, embedded, and pink bounds match within renderer precision.

visualVerdict.evidence: The embedded view restores the original cap red/white spot layout and stem coloration that the uniform vertex-color comparator cannot represent; the pink comparator confirms the map contribution is removed. The 512 atlas visibly introduces jagged high-frequency spot edges, especially around the large front spot and rear spots.

limitations: This is an isolated prototype; runtime loader/material/export integration was not changed.
The result is a visual comparison, not a pixel-difference or perceptual score.
One 512x512 atlas experiment was run; no tuning loop was performed. The visible aliasing remains a fidelity limitation for this bounded prototype.
